name: Daniel Fernández-Kranz
tagline: Associate Professor of Economics, IE University
intro: I am Associate (Tenured) Professor of Economics at IE University School of Politics, Economics and Global Affairs (SPEGA), Madrid. I am also a Research Fellow at IZA&LISER and a member of the International Health Economics Association.

I am an empirical microeconomist working on the economics of the family, gender, health, and public policy evaluation. I combine administrative data and large-scale survey data to analyze the impact of public policies on gender outcomes — with a particular focus on labor market behaviour, health, marriage, and fertility decisions. I am also interested in how policies and social contexts shape gender norms and their effect on marriage, fertility, and well-being.
You can find my Google Scholar profile here, my ResearchGate profile here, and my ORCID record here.
To learn more about our department's research and seminar series, visit the IE Economics Research Group website.

news.html: New IZA & LISER discussion paper: “Childhood Exposure to Joint Custody Reforms and Adult Family Formation” (with Sébastien Fontenay), featured in What we are reading by the Strengthening Families Research Initiative, University of Notre Dame.

Two papers out this year: “Alimony and Marital Commitment: the Unintended Consequences of Alimony Reform on Assortative Matching” (with Jennifer Roff) in the Review of Economics of the Household, and “Bargaining under Threats: The Effect of Joint Custody Laws on Intimate Partner Violence” (with Natalia Nollenberger and Jennifer Roff) in the American Journal of Health Economics.

Visiting researcher at Monash University (host: David Johnston) and Kyoto University (host: Jay Kang), presenting “Maternity Benefits, Labor Supply and Consumption: Evidence from Bank Transaction Data” (with Libertad González, Alberto Graziano and Josep Mestres), also presented at ASSA 2026 (Philadelphia) and ESPE 2026 (Helsinki).

“High Speed Internet and the Widening Gender Gap in Adolescent Mental Health” (Journal of Health Economics) received the IE Research Sustainability Award for Best Published Paper, and “Bargaining under Threats” received the 2025 Ned Holstein Shared Parenting Research Best Paper Award.

New working paper “Freed from the Boys: How Single-Sex Schooling Shapes Girls' Effort and Performance in High-Stakes Exams” (with Caterina Calsamiglia, Yarine Fawaz and Junhee Lee), IZA DP 18208 and CEPR DP 21477. Revise and resubmit at the Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization.
